title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 5
paragraphs: When Darius was dead, the kingdom passed to his son Xerxes. At first, Xerxes was not at all eager to march against Greece; he was only gathering forces against Egypt. But Mardonius son of Gobryas, a cousin of Xerxes — his mother was Darius's sister — was continually at his side, and having more influence over him than any other Persian, he kept up this kind of talk: “Master, it is not fitting that the Athenians, who have done very great evil to the Persians, should go unpunished for what they have done. Why not, for the present, do what you already have in hand? Once you have tamed Egypt, which has insolently rebelled against us, then lead an army against Athens, so that men may speak well of you and that in future anyone may beware of invading your land.” Such was his argument about revenge, and to it he would add that Europe was a most beautiful country, bearing every kind of cultivated fruit tree, of excellent fertility, and such that the king alone of all mortals was worthy to possess it.
